content.title: About
content.content: Tuna salad with light mayonnaise is a ready‑to‑eat dish where cooked or canned tuna is mixed with a reduced‑fat mayonnaise, fresh vegetables, and sometimes herbs or spices. Light mayonnaise contains fewer calories and less fat than traditional versions, making the salad more diet‑friendly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tuna is one of the richest sources of omega‑3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for heart health.
Light mayonnaise is often made with yogurt or plant‑based oils, lowering saturated fat content.
Athletes and weight‑watchers frequently include tuna salad in their meal plans.
Tuna packed in its own juice retains more nutrients compared to tuna canned in oil.
In Japan a similar dish is called “tuna‑salad” and is commonly used as a filling for sushi rolls.

items.title: Rich in omega‑3
items.content: Omega‑3 fatty acids support cardiovascular health and reduce inflammation.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Tuna provides a complete amino acid profile, aiding muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: Using light mayonnaise cuts the overall calorie count, making the dish suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Tuna supplies B12, niacin, and riboflavin, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The salad contains selenium, phosphorus, and potassium, supporting immune function and electrolyte balance.

items.title: Fish allergy
items.content: People allergic to seafood should avoid tuna salad.

items.title: Mercury content
items.content: Tuna can contain trace amounts of mercury; pregnant women and children should limit intake.

items.title: Sodium in canned tuna
items.content: Canned tuna is often high in salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Quality of mayonnaise
items.content: Some light mayonnaises contain additives; choose versions without artificial preservatives.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the salad chilled as a standalone dish, in sandwiches, wraps, or as a side to vegetable plates. Add cucumber, tomato, fresh herbs, a squeeze of lemon, or a dash of mustard to enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared salad in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, keep the mayonnaise separate from the tuna to prevent the vegetables from becoming soggy.
